rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Wide prompts split by logical move — paragraph breaks = cheapest scan-affordance.
rules_evaluated.evidence: P2 is already split into four move-paragraphs. P3 is one ~55-word paragraph carrying three tightly sequential moves (write close-out content, conditional create-then-update, report back); read-aloud test: the moves are causally chained on one artifact rather than independent, so single-paragraph stays defensible over a mechanical three-way split.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Body lead-in mirrors prompt's opening phrasing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: P3's body lead-in (L37) "Ask Claude to write the close-out, update the ticket, and report what it wrote." opens with the verb "write", while the prompt's own opening clause (registry close-the-ticket-3) is "Update the ticket: short close-out note…" — opening verb "Update". The lead-in's first move (write) and the fence's first move (update) don't share the same opening verb+noun-phrase, a minor phrasal-congruence miss. P1 (dangling-colon sub-case, exempt per §2a) and P2 (shares verb "reverse-engineer" + noun-phrase "how your/this team handles bugs") both rhyme correctly.
